Here's the page. There are three gaps in square brackets for you to fill in: the birth line number, the hospital number for before 37 weeks, and your name at the end.

---

# Helping your midwife find you

Hello from the Riverside community midwives!

Deb asked me to write this page because I am the midwife who gets lost the most. This is true. I have driven round the same block of flats for 20 minutes. I have followed my sat nav to a chippy. Once I walked into the wrong house because the door was open. The nice old man who lived there gave me a Jammie Dodger, so it was not all bad.

When your baby is coming at 3am, we want to be inside your house fast. A few small jobs now will help us a lot. There is a list at the end that you can tick and stick on the fridge.

## First, the dates

Home birth cover starts when you are **37 weeks** pregnant.

If labour starts **before 37 weeks**, you need to go to the hospital. Please do not wait at home for us. Ring the hospital on **[hospital number]**.

We tell everyone this at the booking visit, but there is a lot to remember that day, so here it is again.

## Calling us when labour starts

1. **Phone the Riverside birth line: [birth line number].** It works day and night. Save it in your phone now, and in your birth partner's phone too.
2. **Please do not ring a midwife's own mobile**, even if you have the number. We might be asleep, on holiday or at another birth. The birth line always goes to the midwife who is on call.
3. **Tell us your full address**, even if we have been to your house ten times. It may be a different midwife on call that night.
4. **Send us your location.** You can send a pin on WhatsApp to the birth line phone, or give us your what3words. If you have never used what3words, it is a free app that gives your front door its own three words. It is very good.
5. **Keep your phone close after you call.** If we are lost, we will ring you.

## Help us find the right door

**Show your number.** Please check we can see your house number from the road. If your house has a name and no number, tell us the number of the house next door. I once looked for "Rosemary Cottage" in a long street of terraces. That was the night my sat nav took me to the chippy.

**If you live in a flat, tell us everything.** We need the name of the block, which entrance to use, which floor, and the buzzer or door code. In Everton I once learned that flat 14 was not next to flat 13. It was in the other building. In the end the dad waved a tea towel from the window, and that is how I found them.

**Porch light on at night, please!** In winter, dark streets all look the same. One light on makes a big difference.

**Balloons are welcome.** One family tied balloons on the gate, like for a party. Best idea ever. I found the house straight away. A tea towel in the window also works, as I now know.

**Is the door open for us?** Tell us on the phone if you are leaving it open. I will still knock and shout hello first. I have learned my lesson.

## Parking

Two midwives come to your birth, and we usually come in two cars. If you can keep two spaces free near your door, we will love you for it.

We carry a lot. There are the gas and air cylinders, the big bag, and sometimes things for the birthing pool. Our arms are tired before we even ring the bell, so the shorter the walk, the better.

**If you live in a permit zone** (there are some around Anfield and Kensington), please ask the council for visitor permits before your due date. Keep them by the front door, ready for our dashboards. We have had parking tickets at births before, and it does spoil the happy mood a little.

If parking on your street is hard, do not worry. Just tell us on the phone where the best place is.

## Inside the house

**Clear the stairs and the hallway.** We will be coming in fast with heavy bags, maybe in the dark. Please move the shoes, the washing basket and the Lego. Especially the Lego.

**Pets in another room, please.** I love dogs, I really do. But I once visited a staffie called Pippin who loved me too much. She jumped on me at every visit and I nearly dropped the Entonox. So please close your pets in another room before we arrive. They can meet the baby later, when everything is calm.

## One last thing

Please do not worry about getting all of this perfect. Nobody is checking, and we have seen every kind of house. The list is only there so we can get to you quickly.

In the Philippines, where I am from, we say the midwife is like family. That is how we want you to feel when we knock on your door. We are coming as a friend.

See you soon!

[Your name] and all the Riverside community midwives

---

## Fridge checklist

Tick these off and stick this on your fridge.

**Before 37 weeks**

☐ We know home birth cover starts at 37 weeks. Before that, we ring the hospital on: ____________

**Get ready now**

☐ Birth line number saved in both our phones: ____________

☐ Our house number is easy to see from the road

☐ Flats only: we know our block name, entrance, floor and door code to tell the midwife

☐ Our what3words are: ____________ . ____________ . ____________

☐ The porch light works

☐ Permit zone only: visitor permits are ready by the front door

☐ We have a plan for where the pets will go

**When labour starts**

☐ Phone the birth line (not a midwife's mobile)

☐ Give our full address

☐ Send a pin on WhatsApp or our what3words

☐ Porch light on

☐ Two parking spaces free if we can

☐ Stairs and hallway clear (shoes, washing, Lego)

☐ Pets in another room

☐ Balloons on the gate or a tea towel in the window (not a must, but your midwife will be very happy)

---

Two things to check before it goes out:

- **Family details:** Pippin and "Rosemary Cottage" are real, and this is going on the Facebook group, so you may want to ask those families first or change the names.
- **Emergency wording:** I only used what was in your notes for the calling steps. Deb may want to add the team's usual line about when to call 999.
